name: Landslide & Debris Flow
description: Evidence-based decision protocol for hillside cracking, sudden mudflows, rockfalls, blocked mountain corridors, and post-slide stabilization.

ls_start.prompt: What is the current phase of the landslide event you are experiencing?
ls_start.context: Landslides range from subtle pre-failure warning indicators to violent high-velocity debris avalanches.

options.text: Early warning signs detected (New cracks in walls/ground, rumbling, sticking doors)
options.description: Pre-failure indicators on hillside slope or around your structure.

options.text: Active landslide or debris flow in progress right now
options.description: Earth, boulders, mud, and trees are actively moving down-slope.

options.text: Slide has just stopped; assessing damage, trapped persons, or secondary slide risks
options.description: Immediate post-slide recovery and secondary hazard mitigation.

ls_early_warning_location.prompt: Where are you observing these landslide early warning signs?
ls_early_warning_location.context: Structural foundation shifting requires different evacuation precautions than mountain roadway anomalies.

options.text: At home / building located on or directly below a hill slope
options.description: Residential or commercial structure on hillside or near a valley floor.

options.text: Traveling along a mountain road or ghat section
options.description: Driving or riding through hill passes or near road cuttings.

ls_early_warning_signs_building.prompt: Which specific warning signs are visible around the building?
ls_early_warning_signs_building.context: Sudden ground seepage and widening tension cracks indicate imminent slope shear failure.

options.text: New widening ground cracks, muddy water springs emerging, or tilting trees/poles
options.description: Slope saturation threshold breached; catastrophic failure imminent.

options.text: Minor interior plaster cracks only, during prolonged heavy monsoon rainfall
options.description: Heightened vigilance, Go-Bag readiness, and route identification.

ls_early_warning_mountain_road.prompt: What road conditions are you encountering ahead on the mountain pass?
ls_early_warning_mountain_road.context: Small rock pebbles trickling down a road cutting are often the immediate precursor to a major rockfall.

options.text: Trickling gravel/pebbles falling from cliff, or small mud patches on asphalt
options.description: Slope shear failure commencing directly above the roadway.

options.text: Culverts overflowing with muddy water, tree branches jamming drainage
options.description: Risk of sudden flash debris dam burst across the roadway.

ls_active_slide_location.prompt: Where are you situated while the mass movement / debris flow is taking place?
ls_active_slide_location.context: Your physical environment dictates whether lateral flight or impact-protective curling is possible.

options.text: Outdoors directly in the vicinity or path of moving earth and debris
options.description: You are exposed on the hillside, slope, or gully floor.

options.text: Trapped inside a building as debris impacts exterior walls
options.description: Mud, boulders, or fallen trees are hitting structural walls.

options.text: Inside a vehicle on a hill road as slide occurs nearby
options.description: Rockfall or mudflow impacting or blocking the mountain road.

ls_active_outdoor_escape_feasibility.prompt: Can you immediately sprint sideways (laterally) out of the debris channel?
ls_active_outdoor_escape_feasibility.context: Debris flows channel down ravines and gullies at 30 to 80 km/h. Moving perpendicular to the flow saves lives.

options.text: Yes, clear lateral path away from the gully onto stable ridge or high ground
options.description: Escape perpendicular to the flow path towards elevated stable ground.

options.text: No escape path; debris is closing in or terrain is too steep to run
options.description: Immediate impact bracing and airway preservation stance.

ls_aftermath_assessment.prompt: What is the primary condition of the post-slide area?
ls_aftermath_assessment.context: Initial landslides frequently destabilize uphill slope masses, triggering deadly secondary failures.

options.text: A river, stream, or valley floor has been dammed by landslide debris
options.description: Water impounding behind mud barrier; massive flash flood threat downstream.

options.text: Persons or homes buried under slide material; secondary slides possible
options.description: Search and rescue required without triggering slope re-failure.

guidance.summary: Widening ground tension cracks and muddy seepage indicate that the slope is on the verge of shear failure.
immediate_actions: EVACUATE IMMEDIATELY. Do not spend time packing heavy household items.
Inform all family members and immediate downhill/uphill neighbors verbally.
Evacuate along pre-planned lateral routes towards a known stable geological ridge or municipal shelter.
Keep away from the toe (base) and the crest (top edge) of the slope.
Report the ground cracks immediately to the District Emergency Operation Centre (DEOC) and Geological Survey of India (GSI) nodal officers.
actions_to_avoid: DO NOT wait until nightfall or until mud starts moving; catastrophic slope failures occur in seconds.
DO NOT walk down into natural gullies, dry stream beds, or drainage valleys which become high-speed debris channels.
DO NOT attempt to divert flowing mud with shovels or sandbags.
preventive_measures: Check on elderly and mobility-impaired neighbors during your evacuation.
Carry only your emergency Go-Bag with identification, medications, flashlight, and phone.

emergency_contacts.name: Geological Survey of India (GSI) Landslide Monitoring

guidance.official_reference: Geological Survey of India (GSI) Landslide Early Warning & NDMA National Landslide Guidelines

guidance.summary: Heavy rainfall in hilly terrain creates saturated soils. Prepare for sudden evacuation if conditions deteriorate.
immediate_actions: Inspect the perimeter of your building twice daily for hairline cracks in soil, retaining walls, or foundation joints.
Ensure your 72-hour Disaster Go-Bag is packed and positioned near the exit door.
Sleep in bedrooms located furthest from the uphill slope if staying in the house.
Listen to local weather warnings and Geological Survey of India (GSI) regional landslide forecast bulletins.
Agree on a designated safe family meeting point on high, flat, stable ground.
actions_to_avoid: DO NOT clear hillside drainage channels with heavy excavation machinery during active downpours.
DO NOT ignore unusual sounds like trees cracking or faint rumbling noises.
preventive_measures: Ensure roof gutters and drains direct water away from the hillside slope face.
Check that neighbors are aware of local evacuation pathways.
guidance.official_reference: NDMA Landslide Preparedness Checklist & GSI Guidelines

guidance.summary: Trickling pebbles and small rock fragments from road cuttings are the primary warning of an imminent major slide.
immediate_actions: STOP IMMEDIATELY. Do not attempt to speed past falling stones or pebbles.
Put the vehicle in reverse or carefully execute a 3-point turn if road width permits, and retreat to a wide, stable section of the road.
Warn motorists behind you with hazard flashers, horn, and hand signals.
Park well clear of steep rock cuttings, overhanging ledges, or narrow blind turns.
Alert the nearest Border Roads Organisation (BRO), NHAI, or local police checkpost.
actions_to_avoid: DO NOT step out of the vehicle directly beneath a cliff face to take photos or inspect fallen rocks.
DO NOT drive across freshly deposited mud or rock debris; it can trigger a sudden slide beneath your vehicle's weight.
DO NOT overtake queued vehicles on mountain hairpin bends.
preventive_measures: Wait at a safe highway rest stop or designated transit camp until road clearance teams officially certify the route.
guidance.official_reference: Border Roads Organisation (BRO) & NDMA Mountain Highway Safety Protocol

guidance.status: DEBRIS DAM BURST WARNING ON MOUNTAIN PASS
guidance.summary: Overflowing culverts jammed with timber and mud create temporary debris dams that burst with extreme force.
immediate_actions: Never attempt to drive or walk through water overflowing across a mountain culvert or dip.
Retreat at least 200 meters away from the drainage channel onto elevated roadway.
If trapped between two active slides on a ghat road, move your vehicle to the mountain cut side (away from valley drop-off) and stay alert.
Prepare to evacuate the vehicle on foot up-slope if water or debris begins pooling around the tires.
actions_to_avoid: DO NOT try to manually unblock jammed culvert pipes with hand tools during torrential rain.
DO NOT stand near the edge of the road looking down into the valley; saturated road shoulders collapse suddenly.
preventive_measures: Notify district administration with exact highway milestone or GPS coordinates.
guidance.official_reference: NDMA Guidelines for Disaster Management in Mountainous Regions

guidance.status: LIFE-OR-DEATH: LATERAL SPRINT AWAY FROM PATH
guidance.summary: Active slide in progress outdoors. Escape PERPENDICULAR to the flow direction onto stable high ground.
immediate_actions: RUN LATERALLY (sideways, across the slope) out of the path of the slide immediately.
Aim for a prominent rock outcrop, stable ridge, or elevated shoulder outside the gully channel.
Drop heavy backpacks, baggage, and obstacles to maximize running agility.
Shout a single loud warning to others in the path as you run sideways.
Once on safe high ground, continue moving further away; debris flows widen as they descend.
actions_to_avoid: NEVER run downhill in the direction of the slide — debris flows travel much faster than human sprinting speed (up to 80 km/h).
DO NOT attempt to cross an active mudflow even if it appears shallow; liquefied mud carries massive boulders and has high density.
DO NOT turn back to rescue livestock or possessions.
preventive_measures: Watch for secondary landslides on adjacent slope faces caused by vibration and soil displacement.
guidance.official_reference: Geological Survey of India (GSI) & NDMA Standard Survival Protocol

guidance.status: LAST-RESORT IMPACT STANCE: TIGHT CURL & HEAD SHIELD
guidance.summary: Escape is impossible and debris is upon you. Protect your skull, cervical spine, and airway.
immediate_actions: DROP to the ground immediately behind any sturdy barrier (tree stump, large anchored boulder).
CURL into a tight fetal ball: Bring knees firmly against your chest.
INTERLOCK fingers behind your neck and wrap your arms tightly around your head and ears.
Bury your face against your knees to prevent mud or rocks from crushing your face or choking your airway.
Hold this tight compact position until all movement, rumbling, and falling rocks cease.
actions_to_avoid: DO NOT remain standing upright where boulders or snapping tree trunks can cause catastrophic impact trauma.
DO NOT scream or open your mouth while mud is churning around you; avoid swallowing saturated debris.
preventive_measures: When motion stops, gently probe around your head for air pockets and begin rhythmic tapping signals.
guidance.official_reference: GSI & International Association of Engineering Geology (IAEG) Emergency Survival Standard

guidance.summary: Trapped inside a building facing external debris impact. Seek interior reinforced shelter away from slope wall.
immediate_actions: Move immediately to the side of the building FURTHEST AWAY from the hillside slope.
If multi-story, move to the second floor (upper level) — mud and debris typically bury the ground floor first.
Take shelter under a strong structural table, heavy workbench, or interior reinforced doorway.
Curl into a ball protecting your head and neck with pillows, cushions, or blankets.
Keep doors to the uphill rooms closed to act as an energy-absorbing baffle against incoming mud.
actions_to_avoid: DO NOT stay in ground-floor rooms that face directly against the uphill slope.
DO NOT look out of windows or open uphill exterior doors during active movement.
DO NOT attempt to run outside into the active debris path if the building exterior is already surrounded by moving earth.
preventive_measures: Once movement halts, assess if downhill exits or second-floor windows offer a safe evacuation path.

guidance.summary: Vehicle caught near active rockfall or mudslide on a mountain roadway.
immediate_actions: If the road ahead and behind is blocked by debris, park close to the inner mountain wall (if no rockfall directly above) or away from the valley cliff edge.
Turn on hazard flashers, engage parking brake, and keep seatbelts fastened.
If small debris hits the vehicle: Duck down below window level and cover your head with coats or bags.
If the vehicle is pushed towards the valley ledge: Unbuckle and exit immediately from the opposite side onto the roadway.
Seek shelter behind a sturdy reinforced concrete parapet or tunnel portal.
actions_to_avoid: DO NOT attempt to ram your vehicle through a moving mudflow or rock pile.
DO NOT park on the outside shoulder of the road overhanging the precipice; soft verges crumble under car weight.
preventive_measures: Keep your car radio tuned to local road transport announcements.
guidance.official_reference: NDMA & Ministry of Road Transport Guidelines for Hill Roads

guidance.status: CRITICAL FLASH FLOOD ALERT: LANDSLIDE DAMMED RIVER
guidance.summary: A landslide has blocked a river or stream. The artificial dam will rapidly breach, causing a catastrophic flash flood downstream.
immediate_actions: IMMEDIATE DOWNSTREAM EVACUATION: If you are downstream of the landslide dam, move to high ground immediately.
Climb at least 30 to 50 meters above the valley floor onto hill flanks.
Warn all riverside villages, bridge workers, and residents downstream immediately.
Report the exact location of the river blockage to the District Magistrate, NDMA, and Central Water Commission (CWC) immediately.
Do not return to riverside plains until hydrologists officially breach the dam controlledly or certify the channel.
actions_to_avoid: DO NOT gather on bridges or riverbanks to watch the blocked water.
DO NOT attempt to walk across the natural landslide dam; it is saturated and can liquefy instantly without warning.
DO NOT ignore sudden changes in river flow: if water suddenly drops to a trickle, the river has been blocked upstream!
preventive_measures: Stay connected with District Disaster Management Authority (DDMA) emergency VHF and wireless channels.
guidance.official_reference: Central Water Commission (CWC) & Geological Survey of India (GSI) Landslide Dam Hazard SOP

guidance.summary: Initial slide has stopped. Extreme caution is required as secondary slides frequently occur on freshly sheared scarp slopes.
immediate_actions: Stay clear of the slide scarp and runout zone; wait for trained NDRF / SDRF search teams with sniffer dogs.
If searching for trapped persons, deploy spotters on high ground to continuously watch the upper slope for secondary movement.
Listen for sounds of trapped survivors (whistles, tapping) and mark locations with fluorescent spray or prominent poles.
Check for downed power lines, ruptured water pipes, and broken domestic gas cylinders.
Report the slide details immediately to 112 with exact geographic coordinates.
actions_to_avoid: DO NOT allow untrained crowds to swarm the slide debris; additional weight can trigger renewed soil liquefaction.
DO NOT re-enter damaged buildings until certified safe by civil structural engineers.
DO NOT drink water from local streams near the slide; sediment and animal carcasses cause acute illness.
preventive_measures: Establish a community cordon line 100 meters away from the slide boundary.
guidance.official_reference: NDRF Landslide Search & Rescue Guidelines & GSI Post-Disaster Protocol
